Photograph: Marwat Akbar/AFP/Getty Images Imran Khan Supporters of Imran Khan start march on locked-down Islamabad Pakistani authorities insist marchers calling for former PM to be released from jail will not reach the capital Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi Mon 5 Oct 2026 11.19 EDT Last modified on Mon 5 Oct 2026 12.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Imran Khan ’s supporters have begun a march to Islamabad to demand his release from jail after efforts by the government to halt the protest failed. The march began in the former prime minister’s stronghold province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in north-west Pakistan on Sunday, according to leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party. Concerns have grown over the health of the 74-year-old former Pakistan cricket captain who has been in prison since 2023. Party colleagues and family claim he is being held in solitary confinement and has been denied visits by his doctor or relatives despite having a serious eye condition and high blood pressure. The government had gone to extreme lengths to try to stop PTI holding the long march, including shutting down Islamabad and barricading the capital’s entrances with shipping containers and sandbags. Khan’s three sisters were among those detained last week on grounds of national security. Two rounds of negotiations between the government and PTI leaders took place over the weekend but broke down when Khan’s allies insisted that he be part of political talks. View image in fullscreen Security officials at a checkpoint in Peshawar, the first major stop on the march by Imran Khan’s supporters. Photograph: Arshad Arbab/EPA Attaullah Tarar, the information minister, accused the PTI of “double standards and hypocrisy”. Thousands of supporters had joined the protest by Monday afternoon and the crowds are expected to grow on the way to Peshawar, the main city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which the marchers should reach by Wednesday. The march is being led by the province’s chief minister, Sohail Afridi, who described those taking part as “Imran Khan’s soldiers”. Pakistan locks down Islamabad as Imran Khan’s party vows to march on capital Read more “I call upon you all to come out, the youngsters to come out for the sake ​of your leader who is sitting in jail,” he said. Khan was prime minister from 2018 to 2022, when he was toppled by a parliamentary vote of no confidence. Since then, he and the PTI have faced mounting government pressure, which culminated in his arrest in 2023. The harassment and detention of other PTI leaders continues. View image in fullscreen Marchers with a banner of Imran Khan, who was toppled in 2022 and is said to be held in solitary confinement. Photograph: Saood Rehman/EPA Khan is widely considered the country’s most popular politician, while the ruling coalition government, which is backed by the military, is facing discontent over an economic crisis and a surge in terrorism. Ministers say the march is illegal and all measures will be taken to ensure it does not break through the capital’s boundaries. Tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed to Islamabad and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa last week, raising fears that Khan’s supporters will be met with state violence. Government politicians falsely claimed that the PTI was allowing militants from the Pakistan Taliban to take part in the march. Opposition leaders fear the prime minister will impose emergency rule on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to stop the march. https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/i.text: New Delhi: India and the Czech Republic are looking to expand defence industrial cooperation, with a focus on technology collaboration, manufacturing capabilities and stronger industrial partnerships. The development provides a wider context for growing cooperation between Indian and Czech companies in the defence manufacturing sector.India and the Czech Republic have been exploring opportunities to strengthen defence industrial relations through technology sharing, joint production, research and development, and capacity building. The India-Czech Joint Defence Committee provides a platform for discussions on existing cooperation and potential areas for further engagement.VTDS and DEUS Automation PartnershipAgainst this backdrop, the technology partnership between Vijayan Trishul Defence Solutions (VTDS) and DEUS Automation a.s., a sister company of the Czech STV Group, highlights the growing role of industrial collaboration in strengthening India's domestic defence manufacturing capabilities.Industry-level ties have also picked up. In August, Vijayan Trishul Defence Solutions (VTDS), which holds a Home Ministry licence to manufacture small arms and ammunition, signed a technology partnership with DEUS Automation, a sister company of the Czech STV Group, under which the Czech firm will supply technology to produce small-calibre ammunition in India.The partnership brings together VTDS's domestic manufacturing ambitions and DEUS Automation's technological expertise, supporting efforts to develop local production capabilities and strengthen industrial cooperation between the two countries.Leadership and Industry CollaborationVTDS is represented by Mr. Sahil Luthra, Founder and Managing Director, and Ms. Prikansha Luthra, Co-Founder and Director.DEUS Automation a.s. is represented by Mr. Alex Černý, Chief Executive Officer and Member of the Board, and Mr. Ondřej Černý, Manager of Sales, Projects & Purchase.The partnership reflects the contribution that company-level collaborations can make towards strengthening industrial ties between India and the Czech Republic, particularly in areas involving technology transfer and domestic manufacturing.Expanding India-Czech Defence CooperationAs India continues to strengthen its domestic defence production capabilities, international technology partnerships can help build local manufacturing expertise and expand industrial capacity.The VTDS-DEUS Automation partnership illustrates how collaboration between companies can complement broader bilateral efforts to deepen defence industrial relations and promote technological cooperation between India and the Czech Republic.
